title: What level of firmness is required for compression therapy in lipedema?
summary:
he purpose of this study is to investigate whether a new flat-knit compression garment is more comfortable for women with lipedema and whether it has an impact on symptoms, quality of life, and adherence to compression therapy.
Twenty women with lipedema who have already been using compression garments for at least one year will receive a new compression garment (CuraFlow®, Bauerfeind AG) for the duration of the study. The garment will be worn for a period of four weeks.
Before the start of the study and again after four weeks, several examinations and questionnaires will be completed. These assessments will include:
wearing comfort of the compression garment,
satisfaction with the garment,
any discomfort associated with compression therapy,
quality of life,
adherence to compression therapy,
and changes in lipedema-related symptoms.
The study procedures include a physical examination, an ultrasound examination, and tissue measurements. Participants will also be asked to complete several questionnaires.
During the study, participants will not be informed of the manufacturer or brand name of the compression garment being tested. However, they will be informed that it is a commercially available product that is provided free of charge by the manufacturer.
Participation in this study is entirely voluntary. Choosing not to participate will not affect medical care, future treatment, or access to compression therapy in any way.
The manufacturer will not receive any personal information about the participants. All study data will be recorded and analysed using a study identification number only.

interventions.name: This is a prospective, single-arm exploratory study. Twenty women with lipedema who are already receiving compression therapy will be switched to a flat-knit compression garment (CuraFlow®, Bauerfeind AG, compression class II) for four weeks. Outcomes after four weeks will be compared with baseline

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Women with lipedema who have been using compression therapy for at least one year, provided that their current compression garment is not the study product
Willingness to wear the study product (two sets of compression garments) as the sole compression therapy for four weeks
Exclusion criteria:
Active malignancy
Diabetic neuropathy
Exudative skin disorders of the lower extremities or active infections
Pregnancy (not because of any anticipated risk to the mother or the unborn child, but due to the potential influence of pregnancy on oedema formation)
Severe comorbid conditions whose symptoms may substantially interfere with the assessment of lipedema-related pain (e.g. recent hip surgery or severe pain caused by lumbar spine disorders)
Inability to provide informed consent
Insufficient proficiency in the German language to understand study information and complete study questionnaires
Participation in another clinical study within the previous four weeks
